payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-24
payload.summary:
**Claude Tag** turns Slack into an agent operating system; **Karpathy** calls it the third big LLM UI shift, and Anthropic staff say it already writes code, merges PRs, and keeps its own thread memory; **Codex**, **Vercel**, **Replit**, and **Shopify** builders all push the same direction: software is getting more headless, more multiplayer, and more native to agents; pricing pressure is getting real as **GLM** gets victory laps, **Box** argues the applied layer wins, and founders fight over where value actually lands; the wild card comes from biology, where **Biohub** pitches open-source tooling plus frontier AI as a serious path from scientific discovery toward engineering.

**Claude Tag** 今天最抢眼，Slack 里直接长出一个能干活的代理位；**Karpathy** 说这像是大模型交互的第三次改版，Anthropic 自己的人则把话说得更直白: 会写代码、会开线程、还会自己盯进度；另一边，**Codex**、**Vercel**、**Replit**、**Shopify** 这几路人马其实在讲同一件事，软件正越来越像给代理准备的底座，不再只服务人类点点点；价格战也开始有火药味了，**GLM** 被高调点名，**Box** 押注应用层，大家争的不是热闹，是价值最后落在哪一层；最出圈的反而不是纯软件，**Biohub** 把开放工具、前沿 AI 和生物学硬绑在一起，这个路数不花哨，但很硬。

sections.headline: **Biohub** bets on open-source biology and frontier AI · **Biohub** 押注开源生物学与前沿 AI
sections.body:
On **No Priors**, **Mark Zuckerberg**, **Priscilla Chan**, and **Alex Rives** frame **Biohub** as a long-horizon tool-building effort, not a moonshot drug company. Their argument is blunt: biology still lacks the shared infrastructure, durable datasets, and reusable software that let machine learning compound in other fields.

The episode’s strongest claim is that frontier AI only matters here if it is paired with frontier data collection. They connect protein models, single-cell atlases, imaging, and measurement tools into a feedback loop: build better instruments, generate new biological data, train better models, and hand the tools back to scientists as open infrastructure.

They also make a sharper philosophical turn than the usual biotech pitch. Instead of talking about one-off discoveries, they describe a path from observational biology toward engineered understanding, where models do not just classify patterns but help explain mechanisms and guide interventions at the level of proteins, cells, and eventually larger systems.

在 **No Priors** 这期里，**Mark Zuckerberg**、**Priscilla Chan** 和 **Alex Rives** 把 **Biohub** 讲得很清楚: 这不是一家冲着单个药物去的公司，而是一套长期工具工程。核心判断也不绕: 生物学到现在都还缺共享基础设施、耐用的数据集，还有能被反复复用的软件，这些东西别的领域早就靠它们滚雪球了。

这期最硬的一点，是他们把“前沿 AI”这件事落到了数据采集上。意思很简单，只有模型不够，还得同时把蛋白质、单细胞、成像和测量设备这些环节一起推上去。先造更好的工具，再拿到以前没有的数据，再训练更好的模型，最后把工具继续开放给科学家用，这才转得起来。

他们的说法也比常见的生物科技叙事更激进一点。重点不在“某个发现”，而在把生物学从观察学科慢慢往工程学科推。模型不只是认模式，而是要帮人理解机制，最后能在蛋白质、细胞，甚至更大的系统层面动手干预。

sections.headline: **Claude** as a persistent teammate, not just an app · **Claude** 不只是应用，而是常驻队友
sections.body:
This is a new paradigm for interacting with **Claude** that is significantly more "inline" with all the other human activity org-wide. Once you do all of the under the hood engineering work to make this "just work" (e.g. across tools, integrations, compute environments, memory, security, etc.), **Claude** basically joins the team in a seamless way - you can talk to it as you would talk to a person and it can help with a very large variety of workloads.

Imo this is the 3rd major redesign of LLM UIUX. The first paradigm was that the LLM is a website you go to, the second was that it is an app you download to your computer. This third one is that it is a self-contained, persistent, asynchronous entity with org-wide tools and context, working alongside teams of humans. It really takes a while to wrap your head around it, but it works and it is awesome.

这是和 **Claude** 互动的一种新范式，它和整个组织里其他人的工作流更“贴边”。只要把底层那堆工程问题真的打通，比如工具、集成、计算环境、记忆、安全这些，**Claude** 就会很自然地加入团队。你可以像跟同事说话那样跟它沟通，它也确实能接住很多不同类型的工作。

在我看来，这算是 LLM UI/UX 的第三次大改。第一阶段是你去一个网站上用模型，第二阶段是把它装进电脑当应用。第三阶段则是它变成一个自洽、常驻、异步运行的实体，带着组织级工具和上下文，跟一群人并排工作。这个转变刚开始确实有点难消化，但它真的能跑起来，而且很好用。

sections.headline: Token pricing fights are really fights over where value lands · token 定价吵成这样，本质上是在抢价值归属
sections.body:
I’ve had the chance to see this ecosystem from the different sides - enterprises, agent startups, data providers, labs. 

The core tension here is that the business models, moats, value exchange, execution playbooks for all players are being figured out in real time.

This debate around token pricing is really a debate over where value will accrue - models, application layer, distribution or other layers.

Expect a lot of strong opinions from the different sides to shape the narrative in their favor.

我有机会从几个不同位置看这个生态: 企业、代理初创公司、数据提供方、实验室。

这里最核心的张力是，所有参与者的商业模式、护城河、价值交换方式和执行打法，都还在实时摸索中。

围绕 token 定价的争论，本质上是在争未来的价值到底沉到哪一层: 模型层、应用层、分发层，还是别的地方。

接下来肯定还会冒出很多立场很重的观点，各方都会努力把叙事往自己那边拽。

sections.headline: **Box** bets the applied AI layer wins the pricing war · **Box** 判断定价战里真正吃肉的是应用层
sections.body:
Good post on the dynamics of AI pricing right now. We’re basically going to see a barbell dynamic on pricing between high cost frontier models and cheap but good open or closed weights models. 

Then the question is how do you maximize efficiency from the frontier models, and get better quality and performance of the cheaper models. That’s where the applied AI layer comes in.

The applied layer can route to the best model at any time given the workload at hand, as well as mitigate either high token costs or worse performance. The closer you are to the underlying workflow, the better you can tune the use of models for a given business process. 

That’s all about understanding the workflows, domain specific FDEs, evals by customer or process, getting data setup well for agents, and more. Overall good for applied AI.

这篇关于 AI 定价动态的文章不错。接下来大概率会出现一种两头分化的价格结构: 一边是昂贵的前沿模型，另一边是便宜但已经够好的开源或闭源权重模型。

接下来的问题就变成，怎么把前沿模型的效率榨到最高，以及怎么把便宜模型的质量和性能调得更好。这正是应用层 AI 要发挥作用的地方。

应用层可以根据手头的工作负载随时路由到最合适的模型，也能对冲 token 成本太高或者性能不够的问题。你离底层工作流越近，就越能针对某个业务流程把模型用法调到位。

这件事最终都落在对工作流的理解、特定领域的 FDE、按客户或流程做 eval、给代理把数据底子打好这些具体活上。总体看，这对应用层 AI 是好事。

sections.body:

So @**Shopify** launched their **UCP CLI** that allows all the products on their stores available via the command line.

I was thinking of interesting use cases for the CLI over the weekend and realized that I can use this to create contextual embedded shops for websites.

So now, you can enter your website and get four HIGHLY relevant shops that you can embed in just one click.

For the buyer using this shop, it's an insanely simple experience since they can click buy and checkout with **Shop** in literally one click.

Available, free to use, NO affiliate revenue at plugthatshop dot com

Feedback welcome!

@**Shopify** 刚推出了他们的 **UCP CLI**，可以让店铺里的所有商品都通过命令行访问。

我周末一直在想这个 CLI 能拿来干什么，后来意识到，我可以用它给网站生成有上下文关系的嵌入式商店。

欢迎反馈！
